    <h1>Neutral kaons</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
The system of neutral kaons is a unique laboratory for studying quantum oscillations and CP violation. In this project we concentrate on a precise measurement of the parameter $\varepsilon$, which characterizes the violation of CP invariance.

## Theory {#theory .unnumbered}

- What are $K^0$, $\overline{K^0}$, $K_S$, $K_L$, $K_1$, $K_2$?

Relate these states to one another, for example: $$\begin{aligned}
        |K_L\rangle &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+|\varepsilon|^2}}(|K_2\rangle + \varepsilon|K_1\rangle),\\
        |K_S\rangle &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+|\varepsilon|^2}}(|K_1\rangle + \varepsilon|K_2\rangle).
    \end{aligned}$$

- Derive the transition probabilities $P_{K^0 \to K^0}(t)$ and $P_{K^0 \to \bar{K}^0}(t)$ in two cases: CP symmetry conserved and CP symmetry violated.

- Compute the mass difference of the neutral kaons $\Delta m$ in the SM. Explain the essence of the GIM mechanism. Estimate the mass of the $c$ quark.

- Assuming CP symmetry is conserved, obtain the expressions for the decay rates $$\begin{aligned}
  R_+ & = \Gamma (K^0\to \pi^- e^+\nu_e), \\
  R_- & = \Gamma (K^0\to \pi^+ e^-\overline{\nu}_e), \\
  \overline{R}_+ & = \Gamma (\overline{K^0}\to \pi^+ e^-\overline{\nu}_e), \\
  \overline{R}_- & = \Gamma (\overline{K^0}\to \pi^- e^+\nu_e).
  \end{aligned}$$ Compute the decay asymmetry $$A = \frac{(R_++\overline{R}_+)-(R_-+\overline{R}_-)}{(R_++\overline{R}_+)+(R_-+\overline{R}_-)} = \frac{2e^{-(\Gamma_S+\Gamma_L)t/2}\cos\Delta m t}{e^{-\Gamma_S t}+e^{-\Gamma_L t}}.$$

An example of pseudo-data for the decay asymmetry is available at [\[1\]](#ref-1). It was generated with $\tau_S=8.954\cdot 10^{-11}$ s, $\tau_L=5.116\cdot 10^{-8}$ s and a value of $\Delta m$ that you have to reconstruct.

From now on we assume that CP symmetry is violated.

A beam of neutral kaons studied at $t\gg \tau_S$ consists mainly of $K_L$.

- Show that $$\begin{aligned}
      \Gamma (K_L\to \pi^+ e^-\overline{\nu}_e) &\propto |\langle \overline{K^0}|K_L\rangle|^2\propto |1-\varepsilon|^2,\\
      \Gamma (K_L\to \pi^- e^+\nu_e) &\propto |\langle K^0|K_L\rangle|^2\propto |1+\varepsilon|^2,
  \end{aligned}$$ and compute the asymmetry $$A = \frac{\Gamma (K_L\to \pi^- e^+\nu_e)-\Gamma (K_L\to \pi^+ e^-\overline{\nu}_e)}{\Gamma (K_L\to \pi^- e^+\nu_e)+\Gamma (K_L\to \pi^+ e^-\overline{\nu}_e)}$$ using the tabulated values.

- Show how this asymmetry can be used to explain to aliens the sign of the charge of the electrons in our atoms.

- Using box diagrams, show that the inequality $\Gamma (K_L\to \pi^- e^+\nu_e)\ne\Gamma (K_L\to \pi^+ e^-\overline{\nu}_e)$ requires the CKM quark mixing matrix to be complex.

- Prove that the ratio of the decay rates is $$\frac{\Gamma(K_L \to \pi^+\pi^-)}{\Gamma(K_S \to \pi^+\pi^-)} \approx |\varepsilon|^2.$$

## Experimental part: pseudo-data {#experimental-part-pseudo-data .unnumbered}

The table gives the data of an experiment. Reconstruct $|\varepsilon|$, taking into account

- the detection efficiency of $\pi^+\pi^-$ in the decays of $K_S$ and $K_L$;

- the contribution of background events.

  Decay                   Number of events   Efficiency (%)   Background (%)
  ---------------------- ------------------ ---------------- ----------------
  $K_S \to \pi^+\pi^-$         12 000              95               1
  $K_L \to \pi^+\pi^-$           72                90               10

  : Experimental data

## Systematic uncertainties {#systematic-uncertainties .unnumbered}

Assuming systematic uncertainties

- of $5\%$ in the number of background events,

- of $2\%$ in the detection efficiency,

estimate $|\varepsilon|$ and give its statistical and systematic uncertainties.
